dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Hi. I have two Cobblestone subscriptions running on the same account: the fortnightly house blend and the monthly decaf.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: I can see both of them. The house blend renews on the 4th and the decaf renews on the 20th.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I do not want any more bags stacking up in the cupboard, I have three unopened already. Put that one on hold until September.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Understood. I will set the hold to begin at the end of July so nothing goes out next month.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I do not want any more bags stacking up in the cupboard. Leave everything else on the account exactly as it is.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Hi, I need to send back the rain jacket from order 4482. Does the return postage come out of my refund?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: We cover the return postage on size issues. Was it the wrong size, or is there a fault with it?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Wrong size, it's too tight across the shoulders. Good, so you cover the return postage on size issues.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Understood. Could you read the order number back to me before I raise the label?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Order 4482. I'll drop the parcel off tomorrow morning.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Sunday I'm batch cooking two soups for the freezer, a carrot and coriander and a spiced parsnip. They both need to be thick enough to stand a spoon in. How many tubs will six litres fill?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Thick enough to stand a spoon in, noted. At 400ml a tub, six litres fills fifteen of them.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Fifteen tubs is plenty. And I do mean it about the texture, thick enough to stand a spoon in, please.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Understood. Shall I put a shopping list together for you?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Please do, but just for one batch. I'll make the parsnip this weekend and leave the other until November.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: One batch it is, then. Three kilos of veg, two onions, a head of garlic and a litre and a half of stock.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Three kilos of veg, two onions, a head of garlic. The veg shop is my first stop on Saturday.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Hello. I've got two Ashgrove orders on the way: the oak desk on order 7731 and the desk chair on order 7802. I need to sort out the delivery days.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Of course. The oak desk is booked for Tuesday the 14th and the desk chair for Thursday the 16th. Does that fit with your week?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Not really. A neighbour can take one of them in, but for the other I must be at home, so it needs to move to a weekend. I hope there is no fee for changing a slot.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: No fee at all. We can move any delivery by up to a fortnight.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Then put that one back to Saturday the 18th, assuming your crews work weekends.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Saturday crews run every week, so that is fine. I will send the amendment through to the depot now.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Brilliant. Send the confirmation over when it's booked.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Bev, we're away in Portugal from Saturday for the week. Any chance Erin could look after Pickle and Nutmeg?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: I am sure she would love to, she has been asking since the summer. College finishes at four, so it would be a teatime visit.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Teatime suits them fine. One pouch per cat in the evening, with dry biscuits topped up when the bowl looks low. They will hear the tin and come running.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Straightforward enough, she can manage that after college. How many pouches will she find in the cupboard?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Ten, in the blue box on the middle shelf. That is two a day for the week, so she will not run short.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: I'll copy that onto our calendar so it does not get lost. Erin can send you a photo each evening if you like.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: She does not need to, but it would be lovely. Everything else is written on the pad by the kettle.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Hello. The battery on my Pemberton cordless vacuum has stopped holding charge and I would like to claim on the warranty.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Sorry to hear that. Batteries are covered free of charge for the first twelve months, and after that there is a parts fee.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: It ran fine until a fortnight ago and now it dies after about four minutes. Does a claim need the original receipt?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: You will not need the receipt, since the order on your account covers it. I can get a collection booked from the address we hold.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: That address is right. The machine is only two months old, so it is comfortably inside the twelve months.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Understood. The driver brings a box with him, so you will not need to find packaging.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: That is handy to know. Book the courier for any morning next week.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I need a car booked for Thursday evening. I get into Terminal 2 at 7:15 and my colleague Dan lands at Terminal 5 at about the same time.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: One vehicle can take you both, provided you meet at one terminal or the other. With three large cases I would suggest the XL, at around forty-six dollars.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: The XL sounds right to me. Have the driver wait at the terminal from a quarter to eight.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Booked from 7:45, and I have added a note about the cases.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Good. Send the confirmation to my phone.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Saturday I'm doing a paella for eight and I want it on the hob, not in the oven. How much rice should I buy?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Eighty grams a head, so 640g for eight, and about three times that in stock. On the hob is fine as long as the pan is wide.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Right, and it is definitely going on the hob, not in the oven. I've got a 700g bag in the cupboard, so the rice is covered.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Heat the stock in a separate pan before it goes in; cold stock stalls the rice and you get a chalky middle.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Hot stock, never cold. I've got the whole afternoon free for this.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I'm cooking a mushroom stroganoff for six on Friday and one of the six doesn't eat dairy. How high should the heat be when the cream goes in?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Keep it at a bare simmer once the cream goes in, and use an oat cream so it stays dairy-free. For six you want 900g of mushrooms, so three 300g punnets.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Oat cream it is, and three punnets. Do bear in mind one of the six doesn't eat dairy, so no butter in the pan.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Then use olive oil for the mushrooms and check the stock cube. Does yours have milk powder in it?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: It doesn't, I read the packet. Everything else is already in the cupboard.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Good afternoon. I'd like a slot at the Year 4 parents' evening for Rosa. Could you tell me whether the meetings run to ten minutes or fifteen?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Let me check the sheet. Mrs Adeyemi has Wednesday the 8th at 4.40, or Thursday the 9th at 5.20, still free.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Thursday the 9th at 5.20, please. Could you tell me whether the meetings run to ten minutes or fifteen?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Thursday the 9th at 5.20 is yours. Rosa's reading record should come along with you on the night.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Noted, we will bring it with us. I appreciate you fitting us in.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I'm scaling up the lemon drizzle traybake for twelve tomorrow and it's written for eight. Can I use golden caster sugar instead of white for the drizzle?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Golden caster is fine there; it only deepens the colour a shade. For twelve, go up by half: 300g flour, 300g sugar, 300g butter and six eggs.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Good. I've got 400g of butter in the fridge, which is plenty, so I won't need to shop. How long does it want in the oven?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Fifty minutes at 170C fan, and slide a skewer into the middle at forty-five to check.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I'll test it with a skewer, then. I'll set everything out on the counter tonight.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I want to send two gifts through Halloway's: a tea hamper going to my brother in Cardiff and a candle set going to a colleague in Leeds.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: We can do both. Gift notes are free, and ribbon wrap is £4 a parcel.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Ribbon wrap on both, then. I need to know whether they will both arrive before the weekend.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: I have added the ribbon wrap to both parcels and flagged them for the packing team this afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I need to know whether they will both arrive before the weekend. Charge the lot to the card ending 3106.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: The wardrobe lands on Thursday in a twelve to four slot and I am stuck in a workshop until six. Do they carry it upstairs, or is it left in the hall?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: I can sit at the kitchen table all Thursday, so someone will be here for it. Dan next door still has our drill, remember.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I'll knock for him on Wednesday evening. Theo gets in on the Sunday and we are building it on the Saturday morning, so there is time to spare.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Plenty of time. I'll dig the step ladder and the dust sheets out of the garage while I am at it.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Good, that is one less thing. The Allen keys are in the kitchen drawer.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Hello, I'd like to get the service and MOT booked in before the end of the month.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Happy to help. I have the Skoda Octavia on your account, and its MOT runs out on the 30th, so the 22nd would suit.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Book me in for the 22nd, then. What time would you want it dropped off?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Any time from eight. It will need to stay with us the full day, and you can collect it after five.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: That's ideal, I need the car back by two to fetch my son from football.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Right you are. I'll pencil the Octavia in for the 22nd of this month.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Sound, thanks for that. I'll drop the keys in the night before.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Dev, the fibre engineer is coming Thursday between eight and twelve and I'm at the depot all day. Do they want the old router handed back on the day?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Lectures till eleven for me, I'm afraid. Maureen is about in the morning though, she's here for the extractor fan.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: That helps. He'll want the cupboard under the stairs and nothing else, so he will not be long.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: You just recycle the old router, they don't take it back. Aisha is off nights, so she'll be asleep upstairs.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Then Maureen can let him in and keep him downstairs.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: I'll leave Maureen a note by the kettle. Say the day back to me and I'll put it in my phone.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Thursday. Right, I'd better get back to the depot.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I fly out of Eastfield early on the ninth and want a parking space for eight days.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: There is Long Stay Blue, a ten-minute walk from departures, and Long Stay Green, with a shuttle every fifteen minutes. Both come to forty dollars for the eight days.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Forty dollars for the eight days is about what I expected. Is the booking refundable if the flight moves?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Yes, you can cancel up to twenty-four hours ahead and get it all back.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Book me into the long stay zone, registration KR19 TVO. I will be dropping off at six in the morning.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Colin, we're away for a fortnight from next Tuesday. Could I ask you to put our bins out and bring them back in while we're gone?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Yes, no problem at all. The lorry comes round about half six on a Tuesday morning, so I put mine out the night before.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Kind of you. I'll deal with the first one myself on the way out, we're off at five that morning.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Right you are. Shall I get Ewan to take the second week?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: If he doesn't mind, that would be grand. I'll leave the side gate unlocked either way.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Our kitchen mixer tap has been dripping since Sunday and it is getting worse. Any chance of a plumber this week?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Ray has a gap on Thursday morning. The mains stopcock for your building sits in the upstairs flat, so he will need access there as well. Let me know who is around on the day.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Graham is upstairs all Thursday, and my brother Tom will be in ours from eight.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Good, that covers both flats. Ray usually rings ahead twenty minutes before he arrives. Which number should he use?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Ring him rather than me, he will be up and about. There's a bucket under it in the meantime.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I'm baking a two-layer chocolate sponge for my nephew's birthday on Sunday and it has to be completely dairy-free. I've got a 20cm round tin and a 23cm round tin. How much batter does each one hold?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Dairy-free is no trouble; use a hard block margarine, not a soft spread. The 20cm holds about 700ml and the 23cm about a litre.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: The 20cm suits me better, I think. Can I bake the sponges on Friday and keep them until Sunday, or will they dry out?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Sift the cocoa in with the flour or you will get lumps, and a double batch gives you two nice even layers.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: A double batch, then. And I do want to stress it, nothing with milk in, not even in the icing.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Understood. Block margarine in the sponge, and a vegan buttercream between the layers and over the top.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Block margarine, vegan buttercream, understood. The candles and the cake board are already sorted.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Morning. I need to shift a booking at Fold and Fringe, ideally to something midweek with Nadia if she has room.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Let me look you up. Your cut and colour is down for Saturday the 4th, and she has the 14th at four or the 16th at eleven.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: The 16th at eleven, then. Does the late-change fee still apply if I give a week's notice?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: The 16th at eleven is yours. Nadia will want about two hours for the pair of services.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: So, does the late-change fee still apply if I give a week's notice? Text me when it's in the diary.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Priya, could we swap Thursdays for the rest of the month? I'm on lates, and Noor would otherwise be hanging about the playground on her own.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Yes, that suits us. Freya swims at four on a Thursday, so I'm at the school gates regardless. Do you want me to run Noor straight home?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: If you would. Noor is in the later group at half four, though, so could you drop her at the pool instead?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Easy enough, the pool is on my way. They want them in the changing room ten minutes early, and those two are hopeless with their kit bags.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Then she will need her kit handed to her at the gate, not left in the car. It's going on the fridge calendar tonight.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Afternoon. The glass carafe on my Bellweather filter machine cracked last night, and the sticker underneath says model 400.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: I can sort that out. The 400 takes the eight-cup carafe and the 600 takes the twelve-cup carafe, so tell me back which one I should order.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: The 400 takes the eight-cup carafe, and that is the one I need. Mine is the 400.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Added to your basket. Delivery runs two to three working days to the address we hold for you.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Good. Let's get it ordered today if we can.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Hi, I'd like to book a cleaning at the Riverside dental clinic. Could you tell me what slots are open this week?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Sure. I have Thursday at 2pm or Friday at 10am available.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Let's take the Thursday one. My mornings are completely booked this week, so that works well. Will I get a reminder?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Yes, a text reminder goes out the day before. I'll put you down for that one.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Perfect, thanks. Can we go ahead and lock that in?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Good morning. I need to book the one-week renewal appointment at the Lancaster Road office.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: I can do that. The earliest is Monday the 13th at 9.15, and there is a later one on Wednesday the 15th at 2.30.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Monday the 13th at 9.15 suits me a good deal better than the Wednesday.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Booked. Bring your current passport, the completed form and one signed photo, and read the date and time back to me.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Monday the 13th at 9.15. My current passport is here in the drawer with the form.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: That matches the slot I am holding, so I have it saved on the system now.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Understood, I will aim to be early. I'll bring the whole folder with me on the day.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I've got two joints in the fridge for tomorrow, a 1.6kg lamb shoulder and a 2kg pork loin. How long does each want in the oven?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: The lamb wants ninety minutes at 160C fan, then fifteen minutes under foil; the pork wants an hour and three quarters at 180C.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Right. I'll do the joint first and get the potatoes going while it rests. Does the oven need preheating?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Yes, give it a good twenty minutes to come up before anything goes in, or the first half hour is wasted.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Twenty minutes of preheating, fine. I'll jot the timings on the board by the hob.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I'm getting the train to Ashfield on Saturday and then on to the Greenbank centre. I'll have a large case with me.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Two buses will get you there. The 184 runs from Ashfield station to the Greenbank centre every twenty minutes, and the 187 does the same trip hourly but stops nearer the entrance.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I'll take the 187 for the shorter walk. Does the fare include the return, or do I pay twice?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: A day ticket covers the return, so you only pay once. The 187 leaves from stand C.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Stand C it is. I would rather not be carrying the case far.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: It is about thirty metres from the lift to the stand. Shall I send you the platform layout?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Please do. I'll text you when I set off.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: We are taking the ferry over to Alderwick on Saturday and want bikes for the afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: There are two hire places on the island: Harbour Cycles down by the slipway, and Coast Bikes five minutes up the hill.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Either would do us. What time does the first boat leave the mainland?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: It goes from Pier Three at nine twenty, and the crossing over takes about fifty minutes.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: We will be on that one. Two bikes, please, from eleven until four.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: I can hold two bikes. Read the hire place and the pickup time back to me so I have it right.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: The hire place at eleven. We will be at the pier for nine, then.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I want to book the 09:12 to Sheffield on Tuesday. Is a seat reservation included in the advance fare?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Yes, a seat reservation is included in the advance fare. The single is twenty-four fifty. Do you want the return leg as well?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Just the outward leg, thanks. Good that a seat reservation is included in the advance fare.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Outward only, then. Could you read the date and time back to me?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Tuesday, the 09:12. Let's get it booked.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Morning. I want to move off pay as you go and onto a monthly pass. Which one should I be on?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: The 31-day pass for zones one and two is ninety-six pounds, which beats the cap of a hundred and thirty-two.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: The pass, then. I start from Bexley Park, which is in zone four, and I travel in five days a week.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Five days a week is where it pays off. Can you confirm the start date and your home station?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Monday the sixth, from Bexley Park. Put it on the card I already have.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Hello. I left a navy suit jacket and a wool coat with you last week, and I need to come in for a fitting.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Of course, both are on the rail. Elif has Friday at half four, or Saturday at eleven if the weekend is easier.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Saturday would be easier, actually. What would you charge to shorten the coat sleeves?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Saturday at eleven, then. Shortening the coat sleeves comes to twenty-four pounds in all.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: That works nicely for me. I'll come straight from the office.
